Pickers walk an average of 14 km a shift. The 200 fastest-selling items are stored across all 40 aisles.

The quarterly customer survey has 48 questions and a 4% response rate. A 5-question pilot sent to 1,000 customers got 23%.

Four teams share one staging environment. Last month a broken deploy blocked it for 9 working days.

files.repo/docs/plan-tiers.md:

The Pro plan costs $49 a month and Business $199. 85% of Business customers use only Pro features plus single sign-on.

files.repo/docs/weekend-replies.md:

The web app loads 9 font files, 1.2 MB in total. The design uses two weights of one typeface on every page.

files.repo/docs/polling-customers.md:

Three customers make 55% of all API calls, mostly polling an endpoint every second for changes that happen about once an hour.

files.repo/docs/conference-spend.md:

files.repo/docs/two-factor-adoption.md:

34% of staff have turned on two-factor login. Most of the rest say they do not want to carry their phone for it; hardware keys cost $50 each.
files.repo/docs/reporting-store.md:

files.repo/docs/status-reports.md:

Each team lead spends about 2 hours a week writing a status report. On average 4 of the 60 recipients open it.
files.repo/docs/push-volume.md:

files.repo/docs/interview-rounds.md:

files.repo/docs/japanese-rating.md:

files.repo/docs/payment-phishing.md:

files.repo/docs/van-routes.md:

files.repo/docs/onboarding-calls.md:

files.repo/docs/battery-drain.md:

papers.dpr.md:
# Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

Karpukhin et al. (2020) train two BERT encoders, one for questions and one for passages, and score a pair by the dot product of their vectors. Training uses in-batch negatives plus one hard negative per question retrieved by BM25. On Natural Questions, top-20 retrieval accuracy rose from 59.1% with BM25 to 78.4%.
papers.rag.md:
# Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

Lewis et al. (2020) combine a pre-trained retriever (DPR) with a BART generator. RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved passage for the whole output sequence; RAG-Token may draw on a different passage for each generated token.
papers.fid.md:
# Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering

Izacard and Grave (2021) propose Fusion-in-Decoder: each retrieved passage is encoded independently together with the question, and the decoder attends over the concatenation of all encoded passages. Accuracy kept rising as the number of passages grew to 100.
papers.react.md:
# ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

Yao et al. (2023) prompt a language model to interleave reasoning traces with task-specific actions, such as queries to a Wikipedia API, so that reasoning steers the actions and the observations inform the reasoning.
papers.colbert.md:
# ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

Khattab and Zaharia (2020) encode the query and the passage separately into one embedding per token, and score a pair by summing, over the query tokens, each token's maximum similarity to any passage token (late interaction).
papers.splade.md:
# SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Ranking

Formal, Piwowarski and Clinchant (2021) use a BERT masked-language-model head to map a query or a document to a sparse vector of term weights over the whole vocabulary, including expansion terms that do not occur in the text, with a sparsity regulariser so an inverted index can serve it.
papers.hyde.md:
# Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)

Gao, Ma, Lin and Callan (2022) have an instruction-following language model write a hypothetical document that answers the query, embed that document with an unsupervised contrastive encoder, and retrieve the real documents nearest to it.
papers.contriever.md:
# Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning (Contriever)

Izacard, Caron, Hosseini, Riedel, Bojanowski, Joulin and Grave (2021) train a dense retriever without any relevance labels: two spans cropped independently from the same document form a positive pair, and a MoCo-style queue supplies the negatives for the contrastive loss.
papers.retro.md:
# Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens (RETRO)

Borgeaud et al. (2021) condition a language model on chunks retrieved, by frozen BERT embeddings, from a database of about 2 trillion tokens, and feed them in through chunked cross-attention.
